s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive painful skin lesions and ulcers with systemic symptoms and laboratory abnormalities
salient_findings: Progressive, painful blisters and ulcers of the groin
Enlargement of the tongue with difficulty with mastication
Numbness without weakness of the distal lower limbs
Circinate purpuric patches with erosions on the skin
Hemorrhagic flaccid bullae on the posterior perineum
Macroglossia, glossitis, and a hemorrhagic erosion on the hard palate
key_facts: 1-week history of progressive, painful blisters and ulcers of the groin
3-month history of tongue enlargement leading to difficulty with mastication
3-month history of numbness without weakness of the distal lower limbs
History of IgG λ-type multiple myeloma complicated by anemia and lytic lesions in the calvarium
Patient is taking folic acid and intramuscular cyanocobalamin supplements
Platelet count is within normal range
Prothrombin time is slightly elevated
Activated partial thromboplastin time is elevated
Serum zinc level is low
Biopsy from left groin showed subepidermal blister with chronic inflammatory infiltrate and apple-green birefringence on polarized light microscopy with Congo red staining
Direct immunofluorescence test was negative
Herpes simplex virus PCR from perineal ulcer swab was negative

shortlist.label: Paraneoplastic pemphigus
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive painful blisters and ulcers, history of multiple myeloma, and biopsy findings of subepidermal blister with chronic inflammatory infiltrate

shortlist.label: Multiple myeloma-associated amyloidosis
shortlist.why_kept: History of IgG λ-type multiple myeloma and biopsy findings of apple-green birefringence on polarized light microscopy with Congo red staining

shortlist.label: Bullous pemphigoid
shortlist.why_kept: Subepidermal blisters and chronic inflammatory infiltrate on biopsy, although less likely given the patient's age and lack of typical target antigens

shortlist.label: Zinc deficiency disorder
shortlist.why_kept: Low serum zinc level and skin lesions, although the patient is taking supplements

shortlist.label: Epidermolysis bullosa acquisita
shortlist.why_kept: Subepidermal blisters and chronic inflammatory infiltrate on biopsy, although less likely given the patient's age and lack of typical clinical features

raw.rationale: The patient's history of IgG λ-type multiple myeloma and the presence of subepidermal blisters with chronic inflammatory infiltrate and apple-green birefringence on polarized light microscopy with Congo red staining are consistent with paraneoplastic pemphigus.

rejected.label: Multiple myeloma-associated amyloidosis
rejected.why: While the patient has multiple myeloma, the clinical presentation and biopsy findings are more consistent with paraneoplastic pemphigus than amyloidosis.

rejected.label: Bullous pemphigoid
rejected.why: The patient's age and the presence of subepidermal blisters could suggest bullous pemphigoid, but the association with multiple myeloma and the specific biopsy findings point towards paraneoplastic pemphigus.

rejected.label: Zinc deficiency disorder
rejected.why: The patient's low serum zinc level could contribute to some symptoms, but it does not fully explain the blistering skin lesions and the other clinical findings.

rejected.label: Epidermolysis bullosa acquisita
rejected.why: This condition is characterized by subepidermal blisters, but the patient's age, the association with multiple myeloma, and the specific biopsy findings are more consistent with paraneoplastic pemphigus.
